subject: Reasoning
topic: Syllogism III — drawing valid conclusions from All/Some/No premises
description: Syllogism questions: two or three universal/particular/negative premises — determine which conclusions I and II follow. Standard IBPS PO/Clerk format with definite (not possibility-based) conclusions.

questions.stem:
Statements: All dogs are animals. All animals are living beings.
Conclusion I: All dogs are living beings.
Conclusion II: All living beings are dogs.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion I follows — transitive chain: dogs→animals→living beings, not the reverse
Only Conclusion II follows — reversal of I is not warranted by the given premises
Both Conclusions I and II follow — II would require all living beings to be dogs, not stated
Neither conclusion follows — in fact I does follow via the transitive universal chain

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION I: All dogs are animals (premise 1) + All animals are living beings (premise 2) → All dogs are living beings (BARBARA syllogism — AAA: All A are B; All B are C; therefore All A are C) ✓. CONCLUSION II: 'All living beings are dogs' — the CONVERSE of 'All A are B' is only 'Some B are A' (not 'All B are A'). We can say 'Some living beings are dogs' but NOT 'All living beings are dogs.' RULE: Universal (A-type) conversion — 'All A are B' converts to 'Some B are A' only (partial). PARTICULAR (I-type) conversion: 'Some A are B' converts to 'Some B are A' (symmetric). PYQ FREQUENCY: AAA transitive syllogism in IBPS PO/Clerk prelims, SBI Clerk — the most basic type, appears in every exam.

questions.stem:
Statements: No cat is a dog. Some dogs are black.
Conclusion I: No cat is black.
Conclusion II: Some black things are dogs.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion II follows — II is a valid conversion; I cannot be derived from the premises
Only Conclusion I follows — I incorrectly extends the no-cat-is-dog to no-cat-is-black
Both Conclusions I and II follow — I is not derivable; only II is valid here
Neither conclusion follows — II is a direct valid conversion of some dogs are black

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION II: 'Some dogs are black' (I-type) converts to 'Some black things are dogs' ✓ (I-type conversion is symmetric and always valid). CONCLUSION I: To prove 'No cat is black,' we need a chain: No cat is a dog (E) + Some dogs are black (I). The SOME in premise 2 means only SOME dogs are black — those specific dogs may or may not overlap with the non-cats. Cats can independently be black (there is no premise ruling it out). Conclusion I does NOT follow. RULE: E (No A is B) + I (Some B are C) → No definite conclusion about A and C. EXAM TRAP: Students try to extend 'no cat is a dog' across 'some dogs are black' — the SOME blocks this extension. PYQ FREQUENCY: E+I premise type in IBPS PO Prelims, SBI Clerk prelims — very common trap question.

questions.stem:
Statements: All flowers are trees. No tree is a mountain.
Conclusion I: No flower is a mountain.
Conclusion II: Some mountains are not flowers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Both Conclusions I and II follow — I is valid by AE chain; II follows directly from I
Only Conclusion I follows — II does not follow independently from these premises
Only Conclusion II follows — I is too strong and cannot be derived from an AE combination
Neither conclusion follows — an A+E combination yields no conclusion about flowers and mountains

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION I: All flowers are trees (A) + No tree is a mountain (E) → No flower is a mountain (E) ✓. RULE: A (All A are B) + E (No B is C) → E (No A is C). All flowers are trees; no trees are mountains; therefore no flower can be a mountain. CONCLUSION II: 'Some mountains are not flowers' — since 'No flower is a mountain' (from I), all mountains are non-flowers, so certainly SOME mountains are not flowers ✓. RULE: 'No A is B' implies 'Some B are not A' (the O-type particular follows from E-type universal when B exists). EXAM TRAP: Students sometimes reject II as 'not directly from premises' — but if I is valid and II is implied by I, then II also follows. PYQ FREQUENCY: AE → E syllogism and its O-type corollary in IBPS PO, SBI PO Prelims — 1-2× per sitting.

questions.stem:
Statements: All teachers are doctors. Some doctors are engineers.
Conclusion I: Some teachers are engineers.
Conclusion II: Some engineers are doctors.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion II follows — II is a valid conversion; I cannot be determined from A+I
Only Conclusion I follows — I is an invalid A+I combination giving no definite result
Both Conclusions I and II follow — I requires all doctors to be engineers, which is not stated
Neither conclusion follows — II is a direct valid conversion of some doctors are engineers

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION II: 'Some doctors are engineers' (I-type) converts to 'Some engineers are doctors' ✓ (I-type conversion is always valid). CONCLUSION I: All teachers are doctors (A) + Some doctors are engineers (I) → A+I = no definite conclusion about teachers and engineers. The 'some doctors' being engineers are a SUBSET of doctors — this subset may or may not include any teacher-doctors. RULE: A + I → no conclusion about the first and third terms. CONTRAST: If premise 2 were 'All doctors are engineers' (A), then by AAA we'd get 'All teachers are engineers' and I would trivially follow. But with SOME, we can't commit. MEMORY: 'When two positives are mixed (A+I), the conclusion about the outer terms is uncertain unless BOTH are universal.' PYQ FREQUENCY: A+I → no conclusion trap in IBPS PO/Clerk, SBI Clerk — classic wrong-answer trap.

questions.stem:
Statements: No pen is a book. All books are papers.
Conclusion I: No pen is a paper.
Conclusion II: Some papers are books.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion II follows — II is a valid A-to-I conversion; I cannot be established
Only Conclusion I follows — I incorrectly extends the negation from books to papers
Both Conclusions I and II follow — I only holds if all papers are books, which is not stated
Neither conclusion follows — II is a valid conversion of All books are papers to its I-form

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION II: 'All books are papers' (A-type) converts to 'Some papers are books' ✓ (A → I conversion is always valid). CONCLUSION I: Chain attempted: No pen is a book (E) + All books are papers (A). This gives No pen is a paper ONLY IF all papers are books (i.e., books = papers). But 'All books are papers' means books ⊆ papers (papers is a larger set). A pen could independently be a paper (e.g., a piece of paper is a 'paper') without being a book. RULE: E + A → O-type: 'Some papers are not pens' is valid (valid inference), but 'No pen is a paper' (E about the outer terms) is NOT. EXAM TRAP: This is the most common incorrect extension — seeing E+A and thinking 'No pen is a paper.' The set relationship allows for pens to be papers independently. PYQ FREQUENCY: E+A premise trap in IBPS PO, SBI PO Prelims — 1× per sitting.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some watches are clocks. Some clocks are radios. No radio is a television.
Conclusion I: Some watches are radios.
Conclusion II: Some clocks are not televisions.
Conclusion III: No watch is a television.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion II follows — I is I+I (no result); III is not fully derivable; II is valid via I+E
Conclusions I and II follow — I is an invalid I+I combination with no definite result
Conclusions II and III follow — III cannot be established; watch-to-TV path is incomplete
All three conclusions follow — only II is definitely valid from the given premises

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION II: Some clocks are radios (I) + No radio is a television (E) → Some clocks are not televisions (O) ✓. RULE: I+E → O (those clocks that are radios are definitely not televisions). CONCLUSION I: Some watches are clocks (I) + Some clocks are radios (I) → I+I = no valid conclusion. The 'some clocks' being watches and the 'some clocks' being radios may be completely different subsets. RULE: Two particular (I-type) premises yield no valid syllogistic conclusion about the outer terms. CONCLUSION III: The chain watches → some clocks → some clocks → radios → no radio is TV. Watches connect only to SOME clocks; those SOME clocks may not overlap with the radio-clocks. Cannot say ALL watches avoid TVs. EXAM TECHNIQUE: label premises as A/E/I/O types; then apply rules mechanically. I+I → no conclusion; I+E → O conclusion. PYQ FREQUENCY: 3-conclusion 3-statement syllogisms in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains reasoning sections.

questions.stem:
Statements: All metals are conductors. Some conductors are insulators. All insulators are brittle.
Conclusion I: Some metals are insulators.
Conclusion II: Some brittle things are conductors.
Conclusion III: All metals are brittle.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.option_text: Only Conclusion II follows — II is valid via I+A; I is invalid A+I; III overgeneralises
Conclusions I and II follow — I is an invalid A+I combination with no guaranteed overlap
Conclusions II and III follow — III extends a partial chain to all metals, which is not valid
Only Conclusion III follows — III incorrectly covers all metals from a partial conductor subset

questions.explanation: CONCLUSION II: Some conductors are insulators (I) + All insulators are brittle (A) → Some conductors are brittle (I) → converts to 'Some brittle things are conductors' ✓. RULE: I+A → I (valid); and I-type converts symmetrically. CONCLUSION I: All metals are conductors (A) + Some conductors are insulators (I) → A+I = no definite conclusion. The 'some conductors' being insulators may not include any metal-conductors. CONCLUSION III: metals → all conductors → some conductors are brittle → but SOME, not all. III requires 'all conductors are brittle,' which is not given. EXAM NICHE: This three-statement syllogism tests multiple rules simultaneously — harder format seen in IBPS PO Mains reasoning. SYSTEMATIC APPROACH: (1) Label types: A+I (metals/conductors/insulators). (2) I+A (conductors/insulators/brittle) → II valid. (3) A+I (metals/conductors/insulators) → I invalid. PYQ FREQUENCY: 3-statement, 3-conclusion syllogisms in IBPS PO Mains, SBI PO Mains, RBI Grade-B.
